title: Raymond Burke expelled for playing across the road
summary: Bull cites Raymond Burke being barred for working across the road, and finds it sick that Jim Robinson and George Lewis are told where to play.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: That's what a lot of people say. I haven't heard.

Well, I haven't heard Raymond Burke in person. I've heard him on records. Yeah. And, and he's, he's, from, from what I hear from people who've been here, he's one of the best clarinet players down here now.
Now, he, he's been expelled from the Hall because he worked across the road.

I mean, that, that to me is, the, the fact that people can stand over my, I mean, my idols, if you like to call them that. Mm-hm. I mean, not so much Raymond Burke. The fact that people can tell Jim Robinson and George Lewis and those fellows where they're allowed to or not allowed to play or they're expelled from, from playing at Preservation Hall. And the fact that those same blokes do rely on that place for a living is, to me, a little bit sick. So, in general, my impressions of, of the situation, the way it stands in, in, in the city and, and with Preservation Hall, is a bit of a, a let down, mm-hm, from that point of view. And, er, and see, see, obviously the people who are, are popular, er, with Jaffe, are the ones that Jaffe hires every night. And also, as far as I can see, er, it, it, it's fast turning into a, a, a place where, er, they want to guarantee they make their big money. And the people that make big money, the people who've got, er, er, as that, bloody idiot artist, if you don't mind me swearing on your tape. No, see, I don't want to. She can always shut her ears. The people who have an image, like Sweet Emma, for instance, because she's had a lot of publicity and because she's a little, old, rickety old woman that people like to look at and say, isn't that amazing that a little, old woman like that can play the piano? The people I hear who draw people, he uses regularly, more regularly than other musicians who are better, just so that he's going to get a good crowd, as far as I can see.
